questions.questionText: 25 kg of wheat at Rs 50 per kg is mixed with 15 kg of wheat at Rs 42 per kg. What is the average price per kg of the mixture?
questions.explanation: Total cost = 25 x 50 + 15 x 42 = 1880. Total weight = 40 kg. Average = Rs 47 per kg.
questions.shortcut: Mean price = total cost / total quantity (not the simple average of prices).

questions.questionText: 15 kg of rice at Rs 70 per kg is mixed with 25 kg of rice at Rs 30 per kg. What is the average price per kg of the mixture?
questions.explanation: Total cost = 15 x 70 + 25 x 30 = 1800. Total weight = 40 kg. Average = Rs 45 per kg.

questions.questionText: 20 kg of tea at Rs 50 per kg is mixed with 30 kg of tea at Rs 45 per kg. What is the average price per kg of the mixture?

questions.questionText: 15 kg of wheat at Rs 30 per kg is mixed with 25 kg of wheat at Rs 42 per kg. What is the average price per kg of the mixture?

questions.questionText: In what ratio must sugar at Rs 24 per kg be mixed with sugar at Rs 42 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 31 per kg?
questions.explanation: Alligation: cheaper : dearer = (42 - 31) : (31 - 24) = 11 : 7 = 11:7.
questions.shortcut: Cross-subtract: (dearer - mean) : (mean - cheaper) gives cheaper : dearer.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must rice at Rs 36 per kg be mixed with rice at Rs 60 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 55 per kg?
questions.explanation: Alligation: cheaper : dearer = (60 - 55) : (55 - 36) = 5 : 19 = 5:19.
questions.shortcut: Cross-subtract: (dearer - mean) : (mean - cheaper) gives cheaper : dearer.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must sugar at Rs 45 per kg be mixed with sugar at Rs 70 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 47 per kg?
questions.explanation: Alligation: cheaper : dearer = (70 - 47) : (47 - 45) = 23 : 2 = 23:2.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must rice at Rs 24 per kg be mixed with rice at Rs 42 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 30 per kg?
questions.explanation: Alligation: cheaper : dearer = (42 - 30) : (30 - 24) = 12 : 6 = 2:1.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must rice at Rs 30 per kg be mixed with rice at Rs 50 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 33 per kg?

questions.questionText: In what ratio must tea at Rs 36 per kg be mixed with tea at Rs 60 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 45 per kg?

questions.questionText: How many kg of rice at Rs 40 per kg must be mixed with 20 kg of rice at Rs 60 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 56 per kg?
questions.explanation: Cheaper : dearer = (60 - 56) : (56 - 40) = 4 : 16. Cheaper = 20 x 4/16 = 5 kg.

questions.questionText: How many kg of rice at Rs 36 per kg must be mixed with 15 kg of rice at Rs 60 per kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 46 per kg?

questions.questionText: A vessel contains 60 litres of pure milk. 12 litres are drawn out and replaced by water. What is the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk left = 60 - 12 = 48 litres. Water = 12 litres. Ratio = 48:12 = 4:1.
questions.shortcut: One replacement: pure part left = original - removed; water = removed.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains 40 litres of pure milk. 10 litres are drawn out and replaced by water. What is the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk left = 40 - 10 = 30 litres. Water = 10 litres. Ratio = 30:10 = 3:1.
questions.shortcut: One replacement: pure part left = original - removed; water = removed.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains 100 litres of pure milk. 15 litres are drawn out and replaced by water. What is the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk left = 100 - 15 = 85 litres. Water = 15 litres. Ratio = 85:15 = 17:3.
questions.shortcut: One replacement: pure part left = original - removed; water = removed.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains 80 litres of pure juice. 15 litres are drawn out and replaced by water. What is the ratio of juice to water in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Juice left = 80 - 15 = 65 litres. Water = 15 litres. Ratio = 65:15 = 13:3.
questions.shortcut: One replacement: pure part left = original - removed; water = removed.

questions.questionText: A container holds 80 litres of milk. 20 litres are removed and replaced with water. The same operation is repeated once more. How much milk is left in the container?
questions.explanation: Milk after two operations = 80 x (1 - 20/80)^2 = 80 x (60/80)^2 = 45 litres.
questions.shortcut: Each operation multiplies the milk by (1 - 20/80).

questions.questionText: A container holds 30 litres of milk. 15 litres are removed and replaced with water. The same operation is repeated once more. How much milk is left in the container?
questions.explanation: Milk after two operations = 30 x (1 - 15/30)^2 = 30 x (15/30)^2 = 7.5 litres.

questions.questionText: A container holds 50 litres of milk. 25 litres are removed and replaced with water. The same operation is repeated once more. How much milk is left in the container?
questions.explanation: Milk after two operations = 50 x (1 - 25/50)^2 = 50 x (25/50)^2 = 12.5 litres.

questions.questionText: A container holds 50 litres of milk. 20 litres are removed and replaced with water. The same operation is repeated once more. How much milk is left in the container?

questions.questionText: A container holds 50 litres of milk. 5 litres are removed and replaced with water. The same operation is repeated once more. How much milk is left in the container?

questions.questionText: In what ratio must a 20% alcohol solution be mixed with a 80% alcohol solution to get a 57% solution?
questions.explanation: Alligation: weaker : stronger = (80 - 57) : (57 - 20) = 23 : 37 = 23:37.
questions.shortcut: (Stronger - target) : (target - weaker) = weaker : stronger.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must a 25% alcohol solution be mixed with a 55% alcohol solution to get a 51% solution?
questions.explanation: Alligation: weaker : stronger = (55 - 51) : (51 - 25) = 4 : 26 = 2:13.
questions.shortcut: (Stronger - target) : (target - weaker) = weaker : stronger.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must a 25% alcohol solution be mixed with a 55% alcohol solution to get a 50% solution?

questions.questionText: One vessel has 20 litres of a milk-water mixture in the ratio 4:1 and another has 14 litres in the ratio 1:1. If both are mixed, how many litres of milk are there in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk in first = 20 x 4/5 = 16. Milk in second = 14 x 1/2 = 7. Total milk = 23 litres.
questions.shortcut: Milk = quantity x (milk part / total parts) in each vessel.

questions.questionText: One vessel has 6 litres of a milk-water mixture in the ratio 1:1 and another has 21 litres in the ratio 2:1. If both are mixed, how many litres of milk are there in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk in first = 6 x 1/2 = 3. Milk in second = 21 x 2/3 = 14. Total milk = 17 litres.

questions.questionText: In what ratio must a 15% alcohol solution be mixed with a 45% alcohol solution to get a 28% solution?

questions.questionText: One vessel has 56 litres of a milk-water mixture in the ratio 5:3 and another has 25 litres in the ratio 1:4. If both are mixed, how many litres of milk are there in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk in first = 56 x 5/8 = 35. Milk in second = 25 x 1/5 = 5. Total milk = 40 litres.

questions.questionText: One vessel has 8 litres of a milk-water mixture in the ratio 3:1 and another has 35 litres in the ratio 1:4. If both are mixed, how many litres of milk are there in the mixture?

questions.questionText: How many litres of water must be added to 40 litres of a 40% acid solution to dilute it to a 25% solution?
questions.explanation: Acid = 40 x 40% = 16 L stays fixed. New volume = 16/25% = 64 L. Water = 64 - 40 = 24 L.
questions.shortcut: The amount of acid never changes; find the new total volume, then subtract the old.

questions.questionText: Vessel A has milk and water in the ratio 1:2 and vessel B has them in the ratio 1:1. In what ratio should A and B be mixed to get a mixture with milk and water in the ratio 9:11?

questions.questionText: How many litres of water must be added to 50 litres of a 50% acid solution to dilute it to a 40% solution?
questions.explanation: Acid = 50 x 50% = 25 L stays fixed. New volume = 25/40% = 62.5 L. Water = 62.5 - 50 = 12.5 L.

questions.questionText: How many litres of water must be added to 100 litres of a 24% acid solution to dilute it to a 20% solution?
questions.explanation: Acid = 100 x 24% = 24 L stays fixed. New volume = 24/20% = 120 L. Water = 120 - 100 = 20 L.
questions.shortcut: The amount of acid never changes; find the new total volume, then subtract the old.

questions.questionText: A trader mixes tea costing Rs 20 per kg and Rs 40 per kg in the ratio 1:3 and sells the mixture at Rs 42 per kg. What is his profit or loss percent?
questions.explanation: Cost per kg of mixture = (1 x 20 + 3 x 40)/4 = Rs 35. SP = Rs 42. Result = (42 - 35)/35 x 100 = 20%, a profit.
questions.shortcut: Find the mixture's cost price first; profit % is on that cost.

questions.questionText: A trader mixes rice costing Rs 45 per kg and Rs 65 per kg in the ratio 3:1 and sells the mixture at Rs 45 per kg. What is his profit or loss percent?
questions.explanation: Cost per kg of mixture = (3 x 45 + 1 x 65)/4 = Rs 50. SP = Rs 45. Result = (45 - 50)/50 x 100 = 10%, a loss.
questions.shortcut: Find the mixture's cost price first; profit % is on that cost.

questions.questionText: A mixture of 45 litres contains milk and water in the ratio 4:1. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 3:5?
questions.explanation: Milk = 36 L, water = 9 L. For ratio 3:5, water needed = 36 x 5/3 = 60 L. Add 51 L.

questions.questionText: A mixture of 20 litres contains milk and water in the ratio 3:2. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 1:1?

questions.questionText: A mixture of 85 litres contains milk and water in the ratio 3:2. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 3:5?

questions.questionText: A 12 litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 2:1. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 3:1?
questions.explanation: Water = 4 L stays fixed. Milk needed = 4 x 3/1 = 12 L. Milk to add = 12 - 8 = 4 L.
questions.shortcut: Water stays fixed when milk is added; scale the water by the new ratio.

questions.questionText: A 80 litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 2:3. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 5:2?

questions.questionText: A 35 litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 2:3. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 4:1?

questions.questionText: A 65 litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 4:1?

questions.questionText: A mixture of 80 litres contains 4/5 milk. How many litres of the mixture must be removed and replaced by water so that milk becomes 2/5 of the mixture?
questions.explanation: Milk now = 64 L. Needed = 80 x 2/5 = 32 L. Each litre removed takes out 4/5 L of milk, so removed = (64 - 32) / (4/5) = 40 L.
questions.shortcut: Milk lost = (amount removed) x (milk fraction); set it equal to the required milk drop.

questions.questionText: A mixture of 40 litres contains 3/4 milk. How many litres of the mixture must be removed and replaced by water so that milk becomes 3/5 of the mixture?

questions.shortcut: Milk lost = (amount removed) x (milk fraction); set it equal to the required milk drop.

questions.questionText: A mixture of 40 litres contains 3/5 milk. How many litres of the mixture must be removed and replaced by water so that milk becomes 3/8 of the mixture?

questions.shortcut: Milk lost = (amount removed) x (milk fraction); set it equal to the required milk drop.

questions.questionText: Three varieties of rice costing Rs 36, Rs 50 and Rs 20 per kg are mixed in the ratio 1:1:2. What is the price per kg of the mixture?
questions.explanation: Cost = 1 x 36 + 1 x 50 + 2 x 20 = 126. Quantity = 4 parts. Price = Rs 31.5 per kg.
questions.shortcut: Weighted average of the three prices, weights = ratio parts.

questions.questionText: Three varieties of rice costing Rs 72, Rs 45 and Rs 36 per kg are mixed in the ratio 3:2:1. What is the price per kg of the mixture?

questions.questionText: Equal quantities of tea costing Rs 60 and Rs 20 per kg are mixed. This blend is then mixed with tea costing Rs 50 per kg in the ratio 1:3. What is the price per kg of the final mixture?
questions.explanation: First blend = (60 + 20)/2 = Rs 40. Final = (1 x 40 + 3 x 50)/4 = Rs 47.5 per kg.
questions.shortcut: Treat the first blend as one variety with its own average price.

questions.questionText: Equal quantities of tea costing Rs 24 and Rs 30 per kg are mixed. This blend is then mixed with tea costing Rs 72 per kg in the ratio 1:1. What is the price per kg of the final mixture?

questions.questionText: Equal quantities of tea costing Rs 72 and Rs 60 per kg are mixed. This blend is then mixed with tea costing Rs 36 per kg in the ratio 2:1. What is the price per kg of the final mixture?

questions.questionText: Equal quantities of tea costing Rs 80 and Rs 40 per kg are mixed. This blend is then mixed with tea costing Rs 20 per kg in the ratio 1:1. What is the price per kg of the final mixture?

questions.questionText: Equal quantities of tea costing Rs 24 and Rs 36 per kg are mixed. This blend is then mixed with tea costing Rs 30 per kg in the ratio 3:2. What is the price per kg of the final mixture?

questions.questionText: Equal quantities of tea costing Rs 60 and Rs 36 per kg are mixed. This blend is then mixed with tea costing Rs 20 per kg in the ratio 3:1. What is the price per kg of the final mixture?

questions.questionText: A milkman buys juice at Rs 48 per litre, mixes it with water in the ratio 4:1 (juice:water) and sells the mixture at Rs 48 per litre. What is his profit percent?
questions.explanation: Cost of 1 litre of mixture = 48 x 4/5 = Rs 38.4. Profit = (48 - 38.4)/38.4 x 100 = 25%.
questions.shortcut: Only 4/5 of each litre is juice, so cost per litre of mixture is that fraction of Rs 48.
